what: Oblique trammel / trammel of Archimedes. A two-motor adjustable-angle trammel. Motor A travels with the red carriage and turns a blue rigid bar between two guided pivots. Motor B stays on the gantry and drives a 20T pinion against a 60T turntable, rotating the yellow passive guide. The orange marker traces a different ellipse when that guide changes from 90° to 60°. The mechanism adapts CrispStrobe’s BSD-3-Clause-licensed Ellipsa carriage and bar assembly.
try: Open Examples and choose Oblique, then open the model with its program. The model, Code and Blocks load together. Press Reset, then Run. Reset again before repeating or after manual movement; keep manual overrides off during the experiment.

Watch one forward and one reverse bar turn with the guides at 90°. The orange marker should trace an ellipse whose principal diameters are 96×32 mm. These are geometric predictions; compare them with the visible marker path.

When the bar is home, watch motor B turn the guide to 60°. The native direction probe establishes that this uses a −90° B encoder target. The guide turns only 30° because of its 3:1 reduction. Motor A holds its physical home angle during this change.

Predict whether the new ellipse becomes wider, taller, tilted or merely larger. Observe both complete drawing directions at 60°. Its predicted principal diameters are 103.564×29.663 mm, tilted 66.949° from the fixed X direction. Its bounding box is different from those principal axes.

The finite program returns both inputs home and holds them. On success completed=1 and failed=0. Reload/reset the complete model before another run; independently zeroing an encoder after a manual jog does not restore the physical datum.
why: A lies on the X guide, B lies on a line at angle α, and their separation is 32 mm. If A−B=32(cosθ,−sinθ), B=(32cotα sinθ,32sinθ) and A=(32cosθ+32cotα sinθ,0). The marker is Q=A+1.5(B−A), so Q=(−16cosθ+32cotα sinθ,48sinθ). At 90° the mixed term vanishes. At 60° it shears the ellipse, changing its tilt and principal axes. The native mechanism must actually produce these coordinates; no marker pose is commanded.
matters: The same rigid bar gives a family of output shapes when a guide constraint changes. This separates two jobs: motor A advances the mechanism around its path, while motor B changes the geometry of that path. It also shows why useful motor feedback requires independent output measurement: encoder arrival alone cannot prove that a carriage or marker moved correctly.
question: When the guide changes from 90° to 60°, does the ideal enclosed ellipse area increase because the long principal axis gets longer?
answer: No. For this fixed marker position the mapping matrix is H=[[-16,32cotα],[0,48]] in millimetres. Its determinant stays −768 mm², so the ideal ellipse area is always 768π mm². The major axis grows while the minor axis shrinks. This is an analytic invariant, not a separate physical area measurement.
further: At home θ=0, the passive pivot is at the guide intersection for either setting. That is why the program changes guide angle only after A has returned home, then waits for B to hold before turning A again.

Both carriages have actual end-seat limits at ±40 mm. Their nominal full stroke grows from 64 mm at 90° to 73.9008 mm at 60°. The latter leaves only 3.0496 mm ideal clearance at each extreme. A full revolution reaches the stops at 53.1301°; the supplied experiment does not authorize arbitrary guide angles.

The motor-B shaft has a real external bearing and two full retaining bushes. Its 20T pinion is saved at a 9° key phase; the inverted motor uses ROTOR -9. Replacing that phase with zero causes stock-tooth interference in the development fixture.

The upper passive carriage uses two separate smooth guide rails, and the lower motor carriage also uses two. Their separation supplies physical resistance to roll; the native sliders are not justified by an invisible extra brace.

The saved hub is raised to shorten the paths for both 250 mm motor leads. Route A with a loose loop outside the front of the moving mechanism and B outside the rear of the yellow carrier. Flexible leads and a physical build are untested.

The packaged qualification observes actual body-carried markers in the real compiler/VM/controller/Jolt route, fits a free-centre ellipse to those observations, and checks cold settling, closures, guide angles, gearing, retention and return. The deliberately frozen-output negative case must fail. Browser import and physical hardware remain separate evidence scopes.
formula: LDraw: 1 LDU=0.4 mm, +Y downward. L=32 mm, u=1.5. Qx=(1−u)L cosθ+L cotα sinθ=−16cosθ+32cotα sinθ; Qz=uL sinθ=48sinθ. Principal semiaxes are singular values of H=[[-16,32cotα],[0,48]]. Each carriage amplitude=L/|sinα|. B encoder targets 0°/−90° select nominal guide angles 90°/60°; these are inputs, not measured outputs.
